claims.text: Substrates with varied lattice parameters can impose controlled epitaxial strain on non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi thin films.
Epitaxial strain modulates magnetic exchange interactions in non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi thin films.
Epitaxial strain modulates magnetic anisotropy in non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi thin films.
Strain-induced changes in exchange and anisotropy alter the magnetocaloric response during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Strain-induced changes in exchange and anisotropy alter magnetic hysteresis during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
A 200–300 °C inert-atmosphere anneal can enable controlled epitaxial strain without full recrystallization.
Substrate-induced epitaxial strain modifies the film microstructure.
Substrate-induced epitaxial strain modifies the local magnetic-domain configuration.
The strain-altered anisotropy energy landscape affects magnetic-domain nucleation and propagation.
Changes in exchange, anisotropy, and domain behavior shift the magnetic entropy change.
Films on substrates with optimized lattice mismatch may show an enhanced magnetocaloric effect relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Films on substrates with optimized lattice mismatch may show reduced hysteresis-loop width relative to the as-deposited baseline.
The magnetocaloric and hysteretic changes should correlate with the magnitude and sign of the imposed strain.
The minimally strained as-deposited baseline exhibits bulk-like magnetocaloric response and hysteresis behavior.
Substrate interactions dominate in the specified thin-film and nanoribbon geometries.
